Two years ago I just got totally fed up with my 9-5, paying a ton of taxes and being a slave to the next weeks paycheck. I decided to buy land and go off grid as soon as possible. I make OK money, but I was pretty far from having that magic number range of $30k-$50k it would take to buy 5-10 acres and set up shop with a tiny house, solar, well etc. etc. Realizing that this was going to take some time and planning, I took advantage of low interest rates and bought one of the smallest, most affordable houses in my area. Here I am two years later, still at least another 5 years away from having the money to actalize the dream. But I feel like I'm making progress every day, which keeps me sane as I continue to work within the system.

My financial plan is to save as much as I can, diversified equally into 4 asset classes. It isn't perfect, and I don't always get money into each one each month. I welcome feedback, I never went to school for business or anything like that.

1 - home equity 2 - 401k 3 - cash 4 - physical gold, silver, commodities

I figure once I get to that $30k mark between home equity and cash, then I can sell my house and start seriously shopping for the right piece of land. I'll keep my 25% savings in the 401k case the financial system doesn't implode, because that will be a nice chunk some day. I'll keep the 25% in gold and silver and not touch that in case the system does implode.

I'll still need to work to some capacity, taxes in some of the locations I'm looking at are around $100 a month. Cell phone/internet will be about $100 a month. If I can pull down $500-$700 I'll be able to live ridiculously comfortable.

For now, I spend my time learning how to live with less. I try to do things the way I'm going to have to do them once I'm out there. If I want a loaf of bread, I get my flour out and bake a loaf of bread. I hand grind my coffee beans with a ceramic grinder that should last the rest of my life. If there's something I need, I check Craigslist first to try and get a used version of whatever it is. I dramatically reduced my alcohol and processed food consumption. So, while I'm still paying for predator drones via income tax, I'm spending every day saving and learning the skills to quit.

If you are allowed, you can significantly lower your payments if you raise the deductible up to the amount of your HRA and you wont have to pay the deductible out of pocket. Just so you know the fee for not having health insurance can be no higher than $695 for a single person with no kids, if you don't have on going conditions, you can just eat the fine and save over $5k.

If you raise your deductible, it will lower you payments significantly, remove collision coverage-- just don't be the cause of the accident--if the accident is the other drivers fault, his liability will cover the cost of repairing your car.
